summary: Defines several subcodes for the BGP Cease NOTIFICATION message. They give more detail about why a session was closed, helping operators match events and diagnose peering problems. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: When a BGP speaker closes a peering session, it can include a subcode that explains the reason. RFC 4486 defines eight such codes and guidance for retrying after some of them.

subtitle: Eight reason codes that explain why a BGP speaker is ending a peering session.

tldr.problem: A BGP Cease NOTIFICATION closes a peering session but, without a subcode, gives the neighbor little information about why it ended.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4486 defines eight Cease subcodes for conditions such as administrative shutdown, a prefix limit, connection rejection or resource exhaustion. It also recommends retry backoff after selected subcodes.
tldr.outcome: Operators receive a more specific session-termination reason. RFC 4486 is a Proposed Standard updated by RFC 8203 and RFC 9003.

facts.label: Future assignments
facts.value: Standards Action or Early IANA Allocation

today: RFC 4486 is a Proposed Standard published in April 2006. It has been updated by RFC 8203 and RFC 9003, and it has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why Cease Messages Need More Detail
sections.content:
A BGP speaker that ends a peering session sends a NOTIFICATION with the Cease error code. The code says the session is closing but does not identify the cause.

RFC 4486 defines subcodes that provide more information for correlating network events and diagnosing BGP peering issues. It also recommends backoff when retrying after certain Cease notifications.
sections.plainLanguage: The Cease code tells a neighbor that a session is closing. A subcode gives the neighbor a more specific reason for the closure.

sections.title: The Eight Cease Subcodes
sections.content:
RFC 4486 assigns subcodes 1 through 8: Maximum Number of Prefixes Reached, Administrative Shutdown, Peer De-configured, Administrative Reset, Connection Rejected, Other Configuration Change, Connection Collision Resolution and Out of Resources.

The names cover operator actions, protocol events and resource conditions. For the maximum-prefixes subcode, the notification may also include the address family and the configured upper bound in its Data field.
sections.plainLanguage: Each of the eight numbers represents a different cause, such as an operator shutdown or a prefix limit. The neighbor can use the reason to diagnose the session event.

sections.title: When a Speaker Sends Each Code
sections.content:
If a speaker terminates a peering because received prefixes exceed a locally configured upper bound, it MUST send Maximum Number of Prefixes Reached. The optional data can contain the AFI, SAFI and prefix upper bound.

A speaker SHOULD use Administrative Shutdown, Peer De-configured, Administrative Reset, Connection Rejected or Other Configuration Change for the corresponding local action. It SHOULD use Connection Collision Resolution when a session ends because of BGP's collision-resolution procedure. Out of Resources MAY be used when the speaker runs out of resources, such as memory, and resets a session.
sections.plainLanguage: A speaker must report a prefix-limit closure with its matching subcode. For administrative actions and other listed conditions, the RFC says which subcode the speaker should use.

sections.title: Retrying After Selected Cease Reasons
sections.content:
After receiving Administrative Shutdown, Peer De-configured, Connection Rejected or Out of Resources, a speaker should use a backoff approach when retrying the connection. The recommendation is to behave as though the BGP DampPeerOscillations attribute were true for that peer.

An implementation should set an upper limit on consecutive automatic retries. After reaching that limit, it stops retrying until an administrator intervenes.
sections.plainLanguage: Some Cease reasons signal that an immediate reconnect may not succeed. The speaker should wait between attempts and stop automatic retries after a configured limit.

sections.title: Assigning Future Subcodes
sections.content:
The document defines Cease subcodes 1-8. Future assignments use either Standards Action or Early IANA Allocation, following the procedures in RFC 2434 and RFC 4020.

Each assignment consists of a name and a value. This keeps the numeric code and its stated reason associated in the registry.
sections.plainLanguage: Future subcodes need an approved assignment and a name. This prevents two reasons from being assigned the same number.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The security considerations section states that this extension does not change the security issues inherent in BGP. It adds reason codes and retry guidance, not a new security mechanism.
sections.plainLanguage: The new subcodes do not change BGP's underlying security properties. They explain why a speaker ended a session.

viz.caption: THE CEASE SUBCODES DEFINED IN RFC 4486

items.label: Maximum Number of Prefixes Reached
items.desc: Received prefixes exceeded a locally configured upper bound.

items.label: Administrative Shutdown
items.desc: The speaker administratively shuts down the peering.

items.label: Administrative Reset
items.desc: The speaker administratively resets the peering.

items.label: Connection Rejected
items.desc: A connection is disallowed after transport acceptance.

items.label: Other Configuration Change
items.desc: Reset due to another configuration change.

items.label: Out of Resources
items.desc: The speaker resets a session after resource exhaustion.
